s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders
key_facts: Patient is a young black woman
Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80
P-ANCA titer 1:20
Anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer 141 U
Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy shows mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy shows intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

salient_findings: Painful pimple-like bumps on bilateral lower legs
Ulcers with central eschars and dusky gray borders

Presented with chills and bilateral lower extremity swelling
Recent course of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus
Medical history includes treatment with methimazole and atenolol
Laboratory tests show elevated CRP and ESR
Normal C3 and C4 complement levels
ANA titer 1:80

Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies level 120 U
Punch biopsy shows mid- and deep dermal lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with neutrophils and focal abscess
Second biopsy shows intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls

differentials: Vasculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus
per_call: Vasculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated CRP, ESR, and anti-myeloperoxidase titer, along with systemic inflammation and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated ESR, CRP, and anti-myeloperoxidase titer, consistent with small-vessel vasculitis

shortlist.label: Erythema induratum
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent painful skin lesions with ulceration, consistent with chronic vasculitis

shortlist.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Neutrophilic infiltrate and necrosis of vessel walls on biopsy, consistent with small-vessel vasculitis

shortlist.label: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with ulceration and systemic inflammation, consistent with small-vessel vasculitis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painful lesions, chills, and bilateral lower extremity swelling, along with laboratory tests showing elevated CRP and ESR, and biopsy results revealing intraepidermal and dermal perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate with necrosis of vessel walls, are consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis. The presence of anti-myeloperoxidase (MPO) titer and P-ANCA titer also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: The absence of granulomas in the biopsy results and the lack of upper respiratory tract involvement make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Microscopic polyangiitis
rejected.why: While the patient has a high MPO titer, the clinical presentation and biopsy results are more consistent with a cutaneous vasculitis rather than a systemic vasculitis like microscopic polyangiitis

rejected.label: Erythema induratum
rejected.why: The patient's lesions do not have the characteristic features of erythema induratum, such as recurrent nodules on the calves

rejected.label: Leukocytoclastic vasculitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy results show perivascular neutrophilic infiltrate, the clinical presentation and laboratory tests are more consistent with cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
